title: FlexNeRFer: A Multi-Dataflow, Adaptive Sparsity-Aware Accelerator for On-Device NeRF Rendering
problem: GPUs fail to meet the performance, power, and area requirements for on-device Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) rendering, and existing NeRF-specific accelerators are tuned for a single algorithm, yielding poor efficiency when applied to other NeRF model variants. No hardware exists that efficiently supports the diversity of NeRF frameworks emerging for on-device 3D scene reconstruction.
motivation: On-device AR/VR and robotics applications are rapidly adopting diverse NeRF models, creating demand for a versatile, energy-efficient accelerator that handles multiple dataflows and sparsity patterns across the NeRF model ecosystem.
method: FlexNeRFer is a specialized chip where an internal communication network (called a Network-on-Chip or NoC) reconfigures itself to handle different ways data flows through the computation, allowing the same hardware to adapt to different algorithm styles. Its multiply-accumulate units (the computational cores) can adjust their precision—operating at different bit-widths like 8-bit or 16-bit—based on accuracy needs, and the chip automatically detects sparse data (matrices with lots of zeros) and selects the most efficient storage format at runtime to avoid wasting computation on zero values. Built in 28 nanometer CMOS technology, this combination of flexible routing, adjustable precision, and automatic sparse-data handling enables one chip to efficiently run many different NeRF algorithms.
key_novelty: FlexNeRFer uses a flexible internal network that adapts its data routing and compute precision on-the-fly, automatically selecting the right format for sparse data, so a single accelerator chip can efficiently run different NeRF algorithms that would otherwise each require algorithm-specific hardware.
contributions: FlexNeRFer, an energy-efficient versatile NeRF accelerator supporting multi-dataflow and adaptive sparsity on a precision-scalable MAC array
A flexible NoC architecture that reconfigures to accommodate different computational dataflows required by heterogeneous NeRF models
An optimal sparsity format selection mechanism that chooses the storage format based on sparsity ratio and precision mode at runtime
28 nm CMOS layout implementation showing 8.22–43.3x speedup and 24.15–20.3x energy efficiency improvement over an NVIDIA RTX 2080 Ti GPU

metrics.speedup: 8.22–43.3x over RTX 2080 Ti GPU; 4.28–6.9x over NeuRex NeRF accelerator
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 24.15–20.3x energy efficiency improvement over RTX 2080 Ti; 2.34–7.5x over NeuRex

limitations: The sparsity and dataflow flexibility mechanisms were evaluated only on selected NeRF variants; generalization to all emerging NeRF architectures is not fully demonstrated.
primary_theme: Multi-dataflow sparsity-aware ASIC for diverse NeRF rendering
